categories.name: SSD Storage
categories.tagline: Expand console storage for 100+ GB story installs without constant uninstalls.
categories.description: Curated PS5 and Xbox Series storage picks from 2025–2026 roundups. Internal Gen4 heatsink NVMe for PlayStation, plus a licensed Xbox Expansion Card path—no USB-archive confusion.
categories.consoleAngle: PS5 / PS5 Pro: install a heatsinked PCIe 4.0 M.2 in the expansion bay. Xbox Series X|S: use a Seagate/WD licensed Expansion Card for full-speed installs; USB externals are for media and cold storage only.

products.name: WD_BLACK SN850X 2TB with Heatsink
products.headline: Top pick for most PS5 upgrades
products.summary: Still the default PS5 upgrade in 2026 roundups: factory heatsink that fits the expansion bay, sequential reads up to 7,300 MB/s, and 2 TB that covers a modern story library plus patches.
products.bestFor: Most PS5 owners who want one internal install and forget about it
pros: Heatsink SKU (WDS200T2XHE) fits the PS5 bay without a third-party cooler
Consistently clears Sony’s official speed requirement in reviews
2 TB + 5-year warranty is the sweet spot for large day-one titles
cons: Heatsink model costs more than the bare stick
Xbox Series still needs a licensed Expansion Card for full-speed internal play

products.name: Crucial T500 2TB with Heatsink
products.headline: Best value Gen4 heatsink SSD
products.summary: When the SN850X heatsink is on sale-tax territory, the T500 with factory cooler is the value Gen4 pick reviewers keep naming: up to 7,400 MB/s read and 2 TB of Micron TLC.
products.bestFor: PS5 players who want internal Gen4 speed at a lower street price
pros: Integrated heatsink meets PS5 height/thermal guidance
Often undercuts brand-premium heatsink SKUs at the same capacity
5-year limited warranty and strong sustained write reviews
cons: Street price swings; confirm the heatsink SKU (CT2000T500SSD5)
Less “name brand” shelf appeal than WD or Samsung

products.name: Samsung 990 PRO 2TB with Heatsink
products.headline: Peak Gen4 when brand tools matter
products.summary: Premium pick when you want the fastest mature Gen4 platform with a slim PS5-rated heatsink—especially if Magician tooling or brand support matters to you.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want peak Gen4 reads and a thin official heatsink fit
pros: Up to 7,450 MB/s sequential read on the heatsink SKU
Ultra-slim cooler designed around PS5 bay clearance
Samsung Magician support if you also use the drive in a PC later
cons: Usually costs more per TB than SN850X / T500
Buy the heatsink model (MZ-V9P2T0CW)—bare sticks need a separate cooler

products.name: Seagate FireCuda 530 2TB with Heatsink
products.headline: Best value for heavy write endurance
products.summary: EKWB low-profile heatsink, up to 7,300 MB/s, and class-leading TBW with Rescue Data Recovery Services—strong when you reinstall and archive a lot.
products.bestFor: PS5 owners who reinstall often or keep large capture archives on the console drive
pros: PS5-ready heatsink from Seagate + EKWB
High endurance rating with Rescue Services included
Mature Gen4 performer still widely stocked
cons: Street price sits above the T500 value lane
Not an Xbox Expansion Card substitute

products.name: Seagate Storage Expansion Card 1TB
products.headline: Top pick for Xbox Series installs
products.summary: Official Xbox Velocity Architecture card: plug into the Series X|S slot and play at full console SSD speed—no USB archive workaround.
products.bestFor: Xbox Series X|S players who need more install slots at native speed
pros: Licensed for full-speed Xbox Series gameplay
True plug-and-play—no heatsink install
Quick Resume and Velocity features stay intact
cons: Cost per TB is higher than DIY PS5 NVMe
1 TB fills quickly with modern day-one titles

categories.name: Headsets
categories.tagline: Hear story dialogue and positional cues without drowning the mix.
categories.description: Console-first headset picks emphasizing platform reality: Xbox-certified wireless, PS5 USB/Link options, and a durable wired classic. Comfort, usable boom mics, and honest dual-wireless where it helps.
categories.consoleAngle: Prefer the Xbox (“X”) wireless SKU when you play both consoles—those dongles usually cover PS5/PC too. Wired 3.5 mm works on DualSense and Xbox controllers. Sony Pulse gear is excellent on PS5/Portal but not a dual-console default.

products.name: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 7X Wireless Gen 2
products.headline: Top pick for Xbox + PS5 households
products.summary: Best cross-console wireless pick in current guides: USB-C 2.4 GHz dongle that covers Xbox, PS5, and PC, simultaneous Bluetooth, and up to ~50 hours of battery.
products.bestFor: Households that hop between Xbox and PlayStation
pros: One Xbox-certified dongle that also works on PS5 / PC
2.4 GHz + Bluetooth mix so phone audio does not kill game audio
Retractable noise-rejecting boom and long battery life
cons: App EQ depth is still better on PC than on pure console
Pricier than a simple wired set if you never leave one platform

specs.platformNotes: Xbox / PS5 / PC / Switch via USB-C dongle

products.name: HyperX Cloud III Wired
products.headline: Best value wired console headset
products.summary: Durable wired classic: angled 53 mm drivers, memory-foam pads, aluminum frame, and a clear detachable boom—no battery anxiety on launch night.
products.bestFor: Budget console players who want reliable chat and comfort
pros: Works on PS5 / Xbox / Switch without proprietary dongles
No batteries or firmware drama
Swappable cushions and a tough metal frame
cons: Wired only—cable management is on you
Spatial audio depends on the console/platform software

specs.platformNotes: Controller jack or USB on PS5 / Xbox / Switch

products.name: PlayStation Pulse Elite
products.headline: Best premium for PS5 dialogue detail
products.summary: Planar magnetic drivers, lossless PlayStation Link wireless, retractable AI noise-reject mic—still the best official PlayStation headset if you also use a Portal.
products.bestFor: PS5 / Portal players chasing dialogue detail and Tempest 3D
pros: Planar drivers deliver cleaner dialogue and staging
PlayStation Link works with PS5, Portal, PC, and Mac
Bluetooth dual-connect for calls without dropping game audio
cons: Not an Xbox wireless headset
Bulkier fit than lighter SteelSeries Nova models

specs.platformNotes: Best on PS5 / Portal; PC via Link adapter

products.name: Logitech G Astro A50 X
products.headline: Top pick for simultaneous Xbox + PS5 + PC
products.summary: Base-station PLAYSYNC headset that stays connected to Xbox, PS5, and PC at once, with HDMI 2.1 pass-through for 4K120 VRR living rooms.
products.bestFor: Multi-console setups that refuse to swap dongles every night
pros: Omni-platform base with on-ear system switching
HDMI 2.1 pass-through for 4K120 / VRR displays
Broadcast-quality LIGHTSPEED mic uplink
cons: Premium price vs Nova 7X for similar day-to-day use
Base station needs HDMI routing space behind the TV

specs.platformNotes: Xbox / PS5 / PC simultaneous via A50 X base

products.name: Turtle Beach Stealth Pro
products.headline: Best value when ANC matters
products.summary: Swappable dual batteries, serious active noise cancellation, and Xbox/PS5 multiplatform wireless—strong when the living room is loud.
products.bestFor: Players who want ANC and hot-swap batteries without leaving console chat
pros: Adjustable ANC with stealthy dual-battery swaps
2.4 GHz + Bluetooth dual-connect
Works across Xbox Series and PlayStation
cons: Heavier than Nova 7X for long campaigns
App EQ experience varies by platform

specs.platformNotes: Xbox / PS5 / PC / Mac via included transmitter

categories.name: TVs & Monitors
categories.tagline: Display picks tuned for console HDMI 2.1, VRR, and HDR story nights.
categories.description: Living-room and desk picks grounded in 2025–2026 gaming display tests. Priority: full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1, VRR + ALLM, honest 4K120 console paths, and brightness that matches your room.
categories.consoleAngle: PS5 and Xbox Series X need HDMI 2.1 with VRR/ALLM for the full feature set. A 144 Hz OLED helps PC later, but consoles top out at 4K120. Bright living rooms may prefer Mini-LED over OLED.

products.name: LG C5 55" OLED evo
products.headline: Top pick for couch console OLED
products.summary: 2025 C-series console living-room default: four HDMI 2.1 ports, VRR/ALLM/G-Sync/FreeSync, Dolby Vision gaming, and brighter OLED evo panels than the C4.
products.bestFor: Couch console play in a light-controlled room
pros: Four full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports for console + soundbar
Excellent contrast for cinematic single-player
Mature Game Optimizer with VRR, ALLM, and HGiG
cons: Still not as bright as top Mini-LED sets in sunny rooms
Static HUDs for years raise OLED burn-in risk

products.name: LG UltraGear 27GS75Q-B 27"
products.headline: Best value desk console monitor
products.summary: Sharp 1440p IPS, 180 Hz panel, FreeSync / G-Sync Compatible VRR—excellent HUD clarity under $200 when a huge TV is overkill.
products.bestFor: Bedroom / office console setups where 27" beats a huge TV
pros: Sharp 1440p text and HUDs
High refresh for smoother camera pans
Console-friendly Adaptive-Sync / FreeSync path
cons: Not a 4K living-room TV replacement
HDR is modest compared with OLED / Mini-LED TVs

products.name: Samsung QN90D 65" Neo QLED
products.headline: Best premium for bright living rooms
products.summary: Mini-LED punch that keeps HDR readable with the curtains open, four HDMI 2.1 ports, and a 65" canvas for couch co-op.
products.bestFor: Sunny living rooms that still want 4K120 console gaming
pros: Excellent peak brightness for daytime play
65" shared-view size for couch sessions
Full 4K120 + VRR / ALLM console feature set
cons: Contrast can’t match OLED in a dark room
No Dolby Vision (HDR10+ / HDR10 instead)

products.name: TCL 65" QM8 Mini-LED
products.headline: Best value 65" Mini-LED gaming TV
products.summary: Dense local dimming, Game Accelerator up to 240 Hz VRR, and Dolby Vision—strong brightness-per-dollar when OLED is out of budget.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a bright 65" console TV without flagship OLED pricing
pros: Mini-LED contrast that holds up with lights on
Console-friendly VRR / ALLM gaming features
Often undercuts Samsung Neo QLED at similar size
cons: Processing and motion can trail LG/Samsung flagships
Confirm the exact QM8 / QM851G SKU before buying

products.name: Hisense 65" U8N Mini-LED

144 Hz VRR gaming features for Series X / PS5 paths
Usually priced under flagship Neo QLED / OLED

Smart-TV software polish varies by firmware

products.name: LG B4 55" OLED
products.headline: Top pick OLED when C5 is too much
products.summary: Four HDMI 2.1 ports, Dolby Vision, VRR/ALLM—same console essentials as the C-series with a slightly dimmer panel for less money.
products.bestFor: Dark-room OLED buyers hunting a lower street price than C5
pros: True OLED blacks for cinematic story nights
Full console HDMI 2.1 / VRR feature set
Often the cheapest current LG OLED on sale

Prior-year model—confirm warranty and firmware support

categories.name: Capture Cards
categories.tagline: Record and stream console footage without turning your living room into a PC LAN.
categories.description: Creator picks ranked for honest HDMI pass-through (so your TV keeps 4K/HDR/VRR), USB convenience for laptop streamers, and capture headroom that matches real Twitch/YouTube encode targets.
categories.consoleAngle: PS5 and Xbox Series output HDMI; match pass-through to your display (4K60 vs 4K120). Most live streams still encode at 1080p60—buy 4K capture only if you archive or edit in 4K.

products.name: Elgato Game Capture 4K S
products.headline: Top pick for most new console streamers
products.summary: USB-C capture up to 4K60 with 4K60 HDR/VRR pass-through—clean PS5/Xbox path into OBS without a desktop PCIe slot.
products.bestFor: Most console streamers and highlight editors buying new
pros: 4K60 capture replaces the old HD60 X ceiling
4K60 HDR / VRR pass-through keeps the TV happy
Mature Elgato + OBS ecosystem on USB-C
cons: HDMI 2.0 class—not for 4K120 pass-through setups
Needs a solid USB bandwidth path and encode CPU/GPU

products.name: Elgato Game Capture Neo
products.headline: Best value first capture box
products.summary: 4K60 HDR pass-through while capturing 1080p60—perfect for Discord clips, TikTok, and first OBS streams.
products.bestFor: First-time console clip creators on a laptop
pros: Affordable Elgato reliability with real 4K60 HDR pass-through
USB plug-and-play for PC, Mac, and iPad workflows
Compact enough to travel to a friend’s couch
cons: Capture tops out at 1080p60
Skip it if you already need 4K archives or 4K120 pass-through

products.name: Elgato Game Capture 4K X
products.headline: Best premium for 4K120 living rooms
products.summary: HDMI 2.1 pass-through up to 4K144 with VRR—ideal when Series X / PS5 Pro runs 4K120 and you refuse to drop the TV to stream.
products.bestFor: 4K120 console setups that still want USB (no PCIe install)
pros: HDMI 2.1 keeps 4K120 gameplay intact on the TV
High-frame capture options beyond typical 1080p60 streams
Still portable versus an internal PCIe card
cons: Needs a true USB 3.2 Gen 2 port for full modes
Overkill if you only ever stream 1080p60

pros: Mature driverless workflow with OBS
HDR10 capture option at 1080p60
Often discounted as 4K S takes the spotlight
cons: Superseded by 4K S for new 4K60 buyers
Not HDMI 2.1 / 4K120 pass-through

products.summary: GC553G2 with 4K144 HDR/VRR pass-through, party-chat ports, and high-frame Windows capture—strong Elgato 4K X competitor.

Built-in 3.5 mm party-chat / headset path
USB-C 10 Gbps for modern laptops
